issue_context.title: BUG: groupby with categorical index doesn't include unobserved categories
issue_context.body:
When a grouping by a CategoricalIndex, unobserved categories are not included in the output.

```
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": pd.Categorical([1, 1, 2], categories=[1, 2, 3]),
        "a2": pd.Categorical([1, 1, 2], categories=[1, 2, 3]),
        "b": [4, 5, 6],
        "c": [7, 8, 9],
    }
).set_index(["a"])
gb = df.groupby("a", observed=False)
result = gb.sum()
print(result)
# Should include a row with 3, the unobserved category
#    b   c
# a       
# 1  9  15
# 2  6   9

df = df.reset_index().set_index(["a", "a2"])
gb = df.groupby(["a", "a2"], observed=False)
result = gb.sum()
print(result)
# Should include two rows with 3, the unobserved category
#       b   c
# a a2       
# 1 1   9  15
#   2   0   0
# 2 1   0   0
#   2   6   9
```

review_comments: any particular reason this was moved from above?

Previously, this block was in an `if...elif...elif...` chain where it would be skipped over when the first if was true (namely, when the grouping is specified by a level in the index). Now it's moved out of that chain, so it's always hit when appropriate.
I think this change would make `level` unused in `_get_grouper_for_level`

It is unused in `Index._get_grouper_for_level` but still "used" in `MultiIndex._get_grouper_for_level`. I say "used" because `MultiIndex._get_grouper_for_level` is now never called by pandas. I think that means it should be safe to remove entirely from MultiIndex (or maybe just raise a NotImplementedError?). Or is it possible someone downstream is using this? In any case, I would like to do that in a follow up. Okay to open an issue instead?

any particular reason this was moved from above?

Previously, this block was in an `if...elif...elif...` chain where it would be skipped over when the first if was true (namely, when the grouping is specified by a level in the index). Now it's moved out of that chain, so it's always hit when appropriate.

This happened to work properly because of the issue in #49223. Now that this issue is fixed here, it fails (the result is not sorted even though it should be). The right fix for this looks quite difficult - the main issue is that `grouper` currently utilizes just `sort` but the groupings each look at both `sort` and `ordered` (in the case of categorical). In the case where `sort=False` and `ordered=True`, we'd need to assign the "wrong" codes in the groupings so that we don't have to rely on the grouper sorting to get the correct result. Things get even more complicated in the case of a MultiIndex where some categories are ordered and others aren't. Alternatively, we could look into having the grouper not sort, but that appears to me to be a large change, and more confusing code.

I also think we shouldn't be sorting the groupby values when `sort=False` even if `ordered=True` (see https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/48749#issuecomment-1295255218).
